query: audit-only shadow mode counterfactual policy logging feature flag no decision impact trading system deployment gate off-policy evaluation
content:
**These terms describe a **risk-minimizing deployment strategy** for updating policies or models in high-stakes production systems (especially algorithmic trading or reinforcement learning-driven decision systems).** [[1]](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/shadow-mode-drift-alerts-and-audit-logs-inside-the-modern-audit-loop)

The overall approach uses **audit-only shadow mode** (parallel execution with logging but **no decision impact**) combined with **feature flags**, **deployment gates**, **counterfactual/off-policy evaluation**, to safely test and roll out changes without risking live trading outcomes. [[2]](https://medium.com/@Praxen/before-offline-rl-hits-users-run-these-7-checks-70138d744a3c)

### Core Concepts and How They Fit Together

1. **Shadow Mode (or Shadow Testing / Silent Mode)**  
   Deploy the new model/policy in **parallel** with the production system. It receives identical real-time inputs (e.g., market data) and generates outputs/decisions, but those outputs are **not acted upon**—only logged for analysis. The legacy system continues to control all real decisions. [[1]](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/shadow-mode-drift-alerts-and-audit-logs-inside-the-modern-audit-loop)  
   - **Audit-only variant**: Emphasizes comprehensive logging (inputs, model reasoning, outputs, timestamps) for compliance, without any execution. Useful for regulated environments like trading/finance.  
   - Benefits: Detects drift, bugs, or performance issues in realistic conditions with **zero production impact**. [[3]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests.html)

2. **No Decision Impact + Feature Flags**  
   **Feature flags** (also called feature toggles) act as runtime switches. Wrap the new policy behind a flag set to "off" or "shadow-only" initially. This decouples **deployment** (shipping code) from **release** (activating it). [[4]](https://martinfowler.com/articles/feature-toggles.html)  
   - Flags enable gradual rollouts (e.g., 1% of traffic), kill switches, or audience targeting.  
   - In trading: Prevents catastrophic errors (e.g., the 2012 Knight Capital incident tied to stale flags). [[5]](https://www.growthbook.io/blog/how-to-implement-feature-flags-at-scale)

3. **Counterfactual Policy Logging**  
   Log not just what happened, but **what would have happened** under the new policy. This creates a dataset for offline analysis: "If we had used the new model on this trade sequence, what would the P&L have been?"  
   - Enables **counterfactual evaluation** without rerunning history. [[6]](https://www.truefoundry.com/blog/agent-gateway-series-part-6-of-7-observability-for-non-deterministic-systems)

4. **Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE)**  
   A key ML/RL technique to estimate new policy performance using data logged from the **old** (behavior) policy. Methods include Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS), doubly robust estimators, etc. [[7]](https://medium.com/@Praxen/offline-rl-from-logs-without-breaking-production-934be2a3e09d)  
   - Critical for **trading systems** where live A/B testing can be expensive or risky.  
   - Combine with shadow logs for more accurate estimates before any real impact.

5. **Deployment Gate**  
   Automated or manual checks that must pass before promotion:  
   - OPE metrics meet thresholds.  
   - Shadow mode shows acceptable divergence (e.g., no excessive risk, drawdown, or latency).  
   - Drift/misuse detection, audit log review, compliance checks.  
   - Conservative gates ensure new policies only affect production via canary or staged rollout. [[8]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01567)

### Typical Safe Deployment Pipeline for a Trading System

1. **Develop & Test Offline** — Use historical data + OPE for initial validation.  
2. **Feature Flag + Shadow Deployment** — Deploy new model behind flag in audit-only shadow mode. Route copies of live inputs. Log everything (counterfactuals). [[9]](https://brightlume.ai/blog/shadow-mode-rollouts-ai-agents-pilot-production)  
3. **Monitor & Evaluate** — Compare shadow outputs vs. production. Run OPE. Check for drift, edge cases, regulatory compliance.  
4. **Deployment Gates** — Automated checks (metrics, safety bounds) + human review.  
5. **Staged Rollout** — If gates pass: enable for small % of trades (canary), monitor live impact, expand gradually.  
6. **Rollback/Kill Switch** — Feature flag allows instant disable.  
7. **Clean Up** — Remove old code/flag once stable to avoid technical debt.

### Why This Matters for Trading Systems
High-frequency or algorithmic trading involves real money and regulatory scrutiny. **Shadow mode + OPE** lets you validate on live market conditions without blowing up accounts. It supports continuous improvement (e.g., RL agents adapting to market regimes) while maintaining auditability. [[10]](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/21693277.2025.2582472)

**Tools/Practices**: AWS SageMaker shadow tests, LaunchDarkly/ similar for flags, custom logging pipelines for counterfactuals, and RL-specific OPE libraries. [[3]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/shadow-tests.html)

This pattern is widely discussed in modern MLOps, AI compliance (e.g., EU AI Act audit needs), and production RL for safe iteration. If this is for a specific implementation, architecture diagram, or code example, provide more details!

sources.description:
### Counterfactual replay

`counterfactual_evaluator.rs` answers "what would the runtime have done under policy snapshot X instead of Y?" against a captured trace. The original event stream and randomness transcript are fixed; only the policy snapshot is substituted. The output is a signed counterfactual decision record that ships alongside the original, so operators can audit a containment without ever applying the alternative policy in production.

`counterfactual_evaluator.rs`

extra_sources.title: Shadow mode, drift alerts and audit logs: Inside the modern audit loop | VentureBeat
extra_sources.description:
Teams can discover problems early by comparing the shadow model's decisions to expectations (the current model's decisions). For instance, when a model is running in shadow mode, they can check to see if its inputs and predictions differ from those of the current production model or the patterns seen in training. Sudden changes could indicate bugs in the data pipeline, unexpected bias or drops in performance. [...] A good AI audit log keeps a permanent, detailed record of every important action and decision AI makes, along with the reasons and context. Legal experts say these logs "provide detailed, unchangeable records of AI system actions with exact timestamps and written reasons for decisions." They are important evidence in court. This means that every important inference, suggestion or independent action taken by AI should be recorded with metadata, such as timestamps, the model/version used, the input received, the output produced and (if possible) the reasoning or confidence behind that output. [...] In the fast-paced world of AI, governance must be inline, not an after-the-fact compliance review. In other words, organizations must adopt what I call an “audit loop": A continuous, integrated compliance process that operates in real-time alongside AI development and deployment, without halting innovation.

This article explains how to implement such continuous AI compliance through shadow mode rollouts, drift and misuse monitoring and audit logs engineered for direct legal defensibility.

## From reactive checks to an inline “audit loop”
